findings.location: Paragraph with quote: “To their mutual grief, they found themselves [both] groping for the light, veritable blind guides”.
findings.source_quote: “To their mutual grief, they found themselves [both] groping for the light, veritable blind guides”.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the bracketed emphasis by rendering the bracketed [both] in Indonesian as in the source or keep brackets to show the same editorial emphasis, e.g. “Untuk kesedihan bersama mereka, mereka mendapati diri mereka [keduanya] meraba-raba menuju terang, benar-benar pemimpin yang buta.”
findings.translation_quote: “Untuk kesedihan bersama mereka, mereka mendapati diri mereka [keduanya] meraba-raba menuju terang, benar-benar pemimpin yang buta”. (currently translated without the brackets as “... mereka mendapati diri mereka meraba-raba menuju terang...”)

findings.location: Final quote attributed to Dr. Breed (last content paragraph)
findings.source_quote: “In no other writer,” says Dr. Breed (in the Treasury of Hymn Stories), “are poetry and religion more exquisitely united.”
findings.suggested_fix: The current Indonesian rendering is understandable but slightly awkward. Suggest a smoother idiomatic rendering that preserves meaning and attribution, e.g. “'Dalam penulis lain mana pun,' kata Dr. Breed (dalam Treasury of Hymn Stories), 'puisi dan agama tidak bersatu seindah ini.'”
findings.translation_quote: “Dalam tidak ada penulis lain,” kata Dr. Breed (dalam Treasury of Hymn Stories), “puisi dan agama lebih indah bersatu.”
